name: Kojokelen Valley
near: The village of Kojokelen (Kojo-Kelen) in the valley itself — houses of red and black clay along the Diptyk River (open.kg). Further down the Ak-Buura is the area of the Papan Reservoir.
elev: The village is at about 2230–2250 m: the parking by the red cliffs ~2230 m (vpoxod), the lowest point of the Visit Alay track from Kojokelen is 2244 m; the campsite near Kojo-Keleng ~2760 m per a 2025 tracker (higher up the valley). The jailoo (summer pasture) ~2700 m, the grotto ~3100 m (Central Asia Travel); Jiptyk Pass 4162–4185 m.
short: Kojokelen is the valley of the Diptyk River at the foot of the Alay Range, 95–110 km southwest of Osh, known for its red Jurassic cliffs, a 50 m waterfall, a sacred grotto with an underground pool, and the trek over Jiptyk Pass to Lenin Peak.
desc: The Kojo-Kelen valley lies in a widening of the Diptyk River valley (a left tributary of the Ak-Buura) at the foot of the Alay Range and covers more than 300 km² (open.kg). At the upper edge of the village rise orange-red cliffs of Jurassic age — the “sculptures of Kojokelen”, called the “Three Dragons Gorge” in trekking descriptions (Visit Alay). 3 km from the village is a waterfall about 50 m high that makes rainbows in summer; higher up is a white-pink grotto with a crescent-shaped entrance and a blue underground pool, revered as a holy place (open.kg, Central Asia Travel). The slopes are covered with spruce forests and meadows; Alay Kyrgyz who keep a nomadic way of life live here. The valley is the start/intermediate point of treks over Sary-Bel Pass (~3137–3200 m) and Jiptyk Pass (~4175 m) into the Alay Valley to Sary-Mogol and the Lenin Peak base camp.
guide: Kojokelen impresses with its contrast: the spruce slopes of the Alay and bright red cliffs like a Martian landscape, right above the clay houses of the village. Walk to the 50 m waterfall 3 km from the village — in summer rainbows stand in its spray — and climb to the grotto with the blue underground pool, which locals consider holy: behave there as you would at a mazar (shrine). The valley is good as the start of a three-day trek over Jiptyk Pass (4185 m), from which Lenin Peak and other Pamir seven-thousanders are visible in clear weather — and the finish is already in Sary-Mogol. Overnight in a guesthouse: Visit Alay's has hot showers, electricity and internet. This is not a hyped place — there are few tourists and a lot of hospitality.
see: The red Jurassic cliffs (“Three Dragons Gorge”) at the upper edge of the village; the ~50 m waterfall 3 km from the village; the grotto with a holy spring and a blue underground lake (~3100 m); the Sharpyldak and Chal-Kuyruk canyons; spruce forests and jailoo (summer pasture) (~2700 m) with yurts where you can see felt and kymyz (fermented mare's milk) being made (Central Asia Travel, open.kg, Visit Alay).
skip: You are looking for a “half-hour by car” place — the valley requires at least an overnight and walking. You don't want a remote area: infrastructure is limited to guesthouses, and the road is dirt. You have already seen the red cliffs of Skazka/Jeti-Oguz and have no time for a long trip from Osh.
diff: Walks to the waterfall and red cliffs — easy/moderate (3 km from the village). The Kojokelen — Jiptyk — Sary-Mogol trek: 3 days, 36 km, 2211 m of ascent, “moderate to hard” (Visit Alay). A one-day crossing Sary-Bel — Kojokelen: 12 km, ~5 h, +400/−970 m (vpoxod). A TripAdvisor review calls the approach along the abandoned road one of the easiest treks in the country.
when: June — early September (the Visit Alay trekking season); weather on the trek is usually stable and sunny, +10…+30 °C in the daytime depending on altitude (vpoxod). Jiptyk Pass — summer only. In winter the village is cut off and cold (schoolchildren studied in yurts in winter — Azattyk).
hours: A natural area with a village; no visiting hours or fees found. Guesthouses mostly receive guests during the trekking season (June — September, Visit Alay).
daytime: Morning and early evening light — the red cliffs are especially bright in low sun (editorial). For the crossing to the pass, set out early in the morning.
how: From Osh west along the Osh — Batken — Isfana highway, then by dirt road toward the Papan Reservoir and up the Ak-Buura/Diptyk (Central Asia Travel): ~95–110 km, about 3 h by car (Visit Alay). Alternatives — on foot over the Kosh-Moynok/Sary-Bel passes from the Alay or over Jiptyk from Sary-Mogol.
needcar: Yes: a 4×4 / SUV or a transfer from Osh is needed; no public transport to the village was found in the sources. In the valley — on foot or on horseback.
self: Yes for experienced trekkers with a GPS track and a tent — the route along the old road/trail is easy to follow (TripAdvisor, qdraw 2025). The difficulties are the drop-off from Osh with no public transport and the crossing of 4185 m Jiptyk Pass. A border permit for the valley itself is not mentioned in the sources; for going on to the Lenin Peak base camp it is required.
roadtype: Paved Osh — Batken road to the turn-off, then a dirt road along the river (gorge) to the village (Central Asia Travel, Visit Alay); above the village — a sandy/abandoned road and trails (qdraw 2025, TripAdvisor).
traveltime: From Osh about 3 h by car (Visit Alay); 95–110 km (open.kg / Central Asia Travel). On foot: from the village to the yurt camp below Jiptyk ~3 h; from Sary-Bel Pass to the village ~3–5 h (Visit Alay, vpoxod).
stay: Guesthouses in the village of Kojokelen (hot shower, electricity, internet — Visit Alay); stays in locals' homes on Asia Mountains tours; a yurt camp at the foot of Jiptyk (B&B in a yurt on a Visit Alay tour); camping in the valley up to ~3500 m (TripAdvisor). Names and prices of individual guesthouses not found.
net: Visit Alay lists internet at the Kojokelen guesthouse (probably Wi-Fi). Operator coverage in the valley and on the passes is not confirmed.
entry: No entry fee found — according to the sources found the valley is not part of a protected area (Visit Alay, Central Asia Travel, open.kg).
transfer: There is no separate tariff. The Visit Alay Jiptick Pass Trek package with a transfer from Osh — $220–520/person (2 people — $360/person); the exact price of a one-off taxi Osh — Kojokelen was not found.
bring: Trekking shoes; warm clothing and a rain jacket (Jiptyk at 4185 m is cold even in summer); sun protection; cash in som; a water filter/tablets; offline maps (editorial, based on trek reports). For entering the sacred grotto — modest clothing (editorial).
warn: Remoteness: no regular transport, medical help is far away. Jiptyk Pass (4185 m) is high mountain terrain, cross it only in season and with preparation. The grotto is a pilgrimage site, respect local customs. Clay buildings and red cliffs are prone to rockfall — don't climb the cliffs (editorial).
food: Home cooking of the Alay Kyrgyz at guesthouses; kymyz (fermented mare's milk) on the summer jailoo — tourists are shown how it is made (Central Asia Travel). No cafe in the village found.
reviews: Google Maps: 5/5, 3 ratings (as of 03.10.2026, catalog check). TripAdvisor “Kozhokelen Valley”: 4.0/5, 3 reviews (2015–2016), No. 18 of 23 in Osh. Pros: red and white cliffs, an easy approach along the old road, a view of Lenin Peak from Jiptyk. Con: the last ~12 km to the Alay are “fast but boring”.
p.sum: Kojokelen is a remote valley with no public transport: it is best to arrange a drop-off from Osh (~95 km, ~3–4 h via Ak-Terek — Papan) through CBT Osh or Visit Alay, or arrive on a trek from Sary-Mogol over the Sary-Mogol/Sary-Bel passes. Overnights are in the village's homestays (no signs, arrange through CBT) and the yurt camp below Jiptyk. The best option is the 3-day Kojokelen — Jiptyk — Sary-Mogol trek with an extension to Lenin Peak.

p.iti.0.title: 2 days from Osh
p.iti.0.plan: Day 1: set out by jeep in the morning (3–4 h), walk to the red cliffs, overnight in a homestay. Day 2: the waterfall and the grotto, after lunch — to Osh.
p.iti.1.title: 3 days: Kojokelen — Jiptyk — Sary-Mogol
p.iti.1.plan: Day 1: the drop-off, a taxi to the yurt camp (1000 som). Day 2: Jiptyk Pass (4185 m). Day 3: the descent to Sary-Mogol → Tulpar-Kol/Achik-Tash.
p.iti.2.title: Combinations
p.iti.2.plan: Logical with Sary-Mogol, Tulpar-Kol and Achik-Tash (over the passes). Not connected by road to Kyrgyz-Ata and Taldyk.
p.season: June: snow on the passes. July — August: yurts on the routes, the best time, +10…+30 °C in the daytime. September: fewer people, colder nights. October — May: the village is cut off, treks are closed.
p.budget.economy: A taxi/drop-off through CBT (price on request) + a homestay ~1000 som with meals/day + a taxi to Jiptyk 1000 som ≈ 3000–5000 som/person for 2–3 days without the drop-off
p.budget.comfort: The Visit Alay Jiptick Pass tour $360/person (2 people) or an 8-day trek from $250
p.permits: Not required for the valley. To continue to the Lenin Peak base camp (the zone between Tulpar-Kol and Yukhin Peak) — a border permit (3000 som via tour.too.kg).
p.access: With children — short walks to the cliffs and waterfall; the road is long. For older people — hard because of the road. Stroller — no. Dogs — locals have shepherd dogs, be careful.
